equation_request.abstract:
We show that the depth of quantum circuits in the realistic architecture where a classical controller determines which local interactions to apply on the kD grid Zk where k ≥ 2 is the same (up to a constant factor) as in the standard model where arbitrary interactions are allowed. This allows minimum-depth circuits (up to a constant factor) for the nearest-neighbor architecture to be obtained from minimum-depth circuits in the standard abstract model. Our work therefore justifies the standard assumption that interactions can be performed between arbitrary pairs of qubits. In particular, our results imply that Shor's algorithm, controlled operations and fanouts can be implemented in constant depth, polynomial size and polynomial width in this architecture.

We also present optimal non-adaptive quantum circuits for controlled operations and fanouts on a kD grid. These circuits have depth Θ( k√n), size Θ(n) and width Θ(n). Our lower bound also applies to a more general class of operations.

specification.problem: Depth of quantum circuits restricted to nearest-neighbour interactions on a k-dimensional grid (k >= 2), both in an adaptive model with a classical controller (claimed to match the arbitrary-interaction model up to a constant factor) and in the non-adaptive model, where fanout and controlled operations on n qubits are claimed to have optimal depth Theta(n^{1/k}), size Theta(n) and width Theta(n).
specification.reconstruction_scope: Chosen scope (no experiment_scope supplied): one non-adaptive nearest-neighbour CNOT-fanout circuit on a 2D grid (k = 2), with the tiny explicit instance of an m x m = 3 x 3 grid (n = 9 qubits: one control plus 8 targets), achieving depth 2(m-1) = 4 and size n-1 = 8 CNOTs, together with the light-cone lower bound that shows depth Omega(n^{1/k}) is unavoidable. Outside scope: the paper's main adaptive-model theorem (constant-factor depth equivalence with the arbitrary-interaction model, which presumably uses measurements and classically controlled corrections), the constant-depth implementations of Shor's algorithm, general controlled operations and fanouts in that model, the general non-adaptive circuits for controlled-U operations on a kD grid, and the lower bound for the 'more general class of operations'. The specific construction below is my own proposal consistent with the stated bounds, not a reconstruction of the paper's circuit.

symbols.meaning: total number of qubits in the fanout (1 control + n-1 targets); also width of the circuit
side length of the square grid, n = m^2 for k = 2
grid coordinates of a qubit; linear index i = r m + c
initial value of target qubit i
controlled-NOT with control at grid site u and target at adjacent grid site v
circuit depth (number of layers of disjoint nearest-neighbour gates)
minimum depth of U in the adaptive kD-grid model and in the arbitrary-interaction model, respectively

equations.label: Fanout operation
equations.description: Definition of the n-qubit fanout gate on computational basis states; it extends linearly. \oplus is addition mod 2.
equations.justification: Standard definition of the fanout gate named in the abstract; the abstract names it but does not define it.
assumptions: Fanout is taken to mean the standard CNOT-fanout (classical copy of a control bit onto many targets).

equations.label: Nearest-neighbour grid constraint
equations.latex: \text{a two-qubit gate on sites } u, v \in \{0,\dots,m-1\}^k \text{ is allowed only if } \|u - v\|_1 = 1
equations.description: Only adjacent grid sites may interact; a layer consists of such gates acting on disjoint pairs. Qubit (r,c) carries linear index i = r m + c for k = 2.
equations.justification: The abstract refers to local interactions on the kD grid and to the nearest-neighbour architecture; the L1-adjacency rule is the standard formalisation of this.
assumptions: Finite m^k sub-grid of the infinite lattice; single-qubit gates are unconstrained and not counted separately.

equations.label: Stated optimal non-adaptive resource bounds
equations.description: Asymptotic resources of the paper's non-adaptive fanout / controlled-operation circuits on a kD grid.
equations.abstract_quote: These circuits have depth Θ( k√n), size Θ(n) and width Θ(n)
equations.justification: Directly stated; the k-th root is read as n^{1/k}.

equations.label: Light-cone lower bound
equations.description: In depth d, information from one site can reach at most the (2d+1)^k sites within L1 distance d; a fanout whose control must influence all n qubits therefore needs d = Omega(n^{1/k}). Exact inequality, not just asymptotic.
equations.abstract_quote: Our lower bound also applies to a more general class of operations
equations.justification: The abstract asserts a matching lower bound; the light-cone argument is the standard way to obtain Omega(n^{1/k}) for non-adaptive nearest-neighbour circuits and is consistent with the stated Theta bound. The paper's actual proof and its generalisation are not available.
assumptions: Non-adaptive model (no mid-circuit measurement/classical feed-forward), since adaptive circuits are claimed to achieve constant depth.

equations.label: Proposed row-then-column CNOT fanout on an m x m grid
equations.description: Control at (0,0) with all targets initially |0>. First a chain of m-1 CNOTs broadcasts x along row 0 (sequential, depth m-1); then m-1 layers of m parallel CNOTs broadcast down every column simultaneously. Products are time-ordered right to left. Equality with F_n holds exactly on inputs with all y_i = 0; for arbitrary y_i the same circuit computes a different Boolean map, so the general fanout of eq_1 would need the standard conversion via a clean ancilla copy or a tree of CNOTs that also propagates correctly, which is left outside scope.
equations.justification: My own simple construction meeting eq_2 with depth O(sqrt n) and size n-1, i.e. matching eq_3 for k = 2 up to constants; the paper's actual circuit is not given in the abstract.
assumptions: k = 2, n = m^2, control qubit placed at corner (0,0).
All target qubits start in |0> (clean-ancilla fanout / GHZ-type copy).

equations.label: Adaptive-model depth equivalence (out of scope, stated for context)
equations.description: The paper's main claim: with a classical controller choosing local interactions on the kD grid, minimum depth matches the arbitrary-interaction model up to a constant factor (with polynomial size and width).
equations.abstract_quote: is the same (up to a constant factor) as in the standard model where arbitrary interactions are allowed
equations.justification: Directly stated as the main result; the construction achieving it is not described in the abstract and is not reconstructed here.
assumptions: Adaptive model: measurements and classically controlled gates are allowed within a layer at unit depth cost, as implied by 'a classical controller determines which local interactions to apply'.

registers.name: ctrl
registers.role: Control qubit at grid site (0,0), linear index 0, holding |x>

registers.name: tgt
registers.role: Target qubits at the remaining sites (r,c) of the 3 x 3 grid, linear index i = 3r + c in {1,...,8}, each initialised to |0>

specification.initial_state: |x\rangle_{(0,0)} \otimes |0\rangle^{\otimes 8} on the 3 x 3 grid (n = 9, m = 3); x in {0,1} or a superposition such as (|0>+|1>)/sqrt2 to produce a 9-qubit GHZ state.

steps.description: Row broadcast: apply CNOT_{(0,0)->(0,1)} then CNOT_{(0,1)->(0,2)} sequentially (2 layers), so row 0 holds |x,x,x>.
Column broadcast layer 1: apply in parallel CNOT_{(0,c)->(1,c)} for c = 0,1,2 (1 layer).
Column broadcast layer 2: apply in parallel CNOT_{(1,c)->(2,c)} for c = 0,1,2 (1 layer). Total depth 4 = 2(m-1), size 8 = n-1, output |x>^{\otimes 9}, realising eq_1 on the all-zero target input.
Check against bounds: depth 4 satisfies the light-cone inequality (2d+1)^2 = 81 >= 9 and the lower bound d >= (3-1)/2 = 1; asymptotically depth is Theta(sqrt n), matching eq_3 for k = 2.

specification.measurement: Not required for the (unitary, non-adaptive) construction. For verification only: measure all 9 qubits in the computational basis; for basis input x every outcome bit should equal x, and for input (|0>+|1>)/sqrt2 the outcomes should be all-0 or all-1 with probability 1/2 each.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Verification only: check that all measured bits are equal (and equal to x for a basis-state control); estimate the failure fraction over repeated runs.
assumptions: No experiment_scope was provided, so the non-adaptive 2D-grid fanout with a 3 x 3 instance was chosen as the single smallest useful construction.
The k-th root notation 'k√n' in the abstract is interpreted as n^{1/k}.
Fanout means CNOT-fanout (eq_1); targets are assumed clean (|0>) for the proposed circuit.
The proposed row-then-column circuit (eq_5) is my construction consistent with the stated Theta bounds, not the paper's circuit.
Depth counts layers of disjoint nearest-neighbour two-qubit gates; single-qubit gates are not counted.
missing_information: The paper's construction proving constant-factor depth equivalence between the adaptive kD-grid model and the arbitrary-interaction model (eq_6), including how the classical controller, measurements and corrections are used.
The constant-depth adaptive implementations of fanout, controlled operations and Shor's algorithm, and their polynomial size/width.
The paper's actual optimal non-adaptive circuits for general controlled operations (not just fanout) on a kD grid and the precise constants in Theta(n^{1/k}).
The exact statement and proof of the lower bound and the 'more general class of operations' it covers.
How arbitrary (non-zero) target inputs are handled in the paper's fanout circuits.
